correctness.rationale: Generator identities Lx=-rbx and Lx^2=2D-rb(2-b)x^2 give the exact stationary covariance, whose positive integral yields the finite-window variance. Logarithmic derivative R(b)-mu_tau(b) is strictly increasing for b>1 because R increases and mu decreases, and negative below 1; endpoint poles ensure a unique global minimizer. A strict exponential reweighting bound locates 1<b*<4/3. The monotone likelihood-ratio comparison as tau grows proves b* increases strictly, and implicit differentiation proves a* is smooth with negative derivative. Endpoint asymptotics and long-run cubic minimization are independently reconstructed. checker.py passed 83 numerical assertions, which are only corroborative; dimensions and all quantifiers were checked.

value.rationale: The stochastic-resetting literature asks which reset prescriptions improve measurable transport observables. Mean signed position over a finite experimental window is a natural fluctuation diagnostic distinct from search time and instantaneous spread. A globally unique negative rescaling optimum, its strict monotone drift with window length, and a 15.625 percent asymptotic advantage despite worsening snapshot variance describe a genuine finite-time control tradeoff, not merely a numerical plug-in to a known mean.
